chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Is'haq ibn Ghalib, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Is'haq! How many do you see to be referred to in this Verse: 'And among them is one who blames you with respect to the charities; so if they are given from it they are pleased, and if they are not given from it, then they are full of rage?' Then he said: 'They are more than two-thirds of the people'.
ai.seo_question: Who are the people referred to in Surah At-Tawbah verse 58 regarding charity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the hypocrites described in Quran 9:58 as those whose faith is contingent upon material gain, noting that such individuals constitute more than two-thirds of humanity. This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the Shia scholarly view that the majority of people are driven by worldly desires rather than spiritual sincerity, a trait characteristic of the 'distorted hearts' discussed in the chapter.
